correctness.rationale: Exact elimination of the printed rational coefficient matrix gives t+(231898/2735) sin(t)=0 and fixed linear coordinate ratios. The inequalities 26*pi<B<27*pi and strict convexity on each negative-sine lobe prove exactly 26 positive nonzero roots; odd symmetry gives 53 equilibria total. Exact Routh first-column signs classify every left-half root as unstable dimension two and every right-half root plus the origin as unstable dimension one. The bundled checker independently replays the rational algebra and root bracketing.

originality.rationale: The same-system source derives only a graphical scalar equilibrium relation, lists two nonzero examples, and states that multiple unstable equilibria exist. It does not state or imply the complete count 53 or the 26/27 unstable-index split. Broad published-finding corpus and web searches found no same-system publication or database entry with this classification. The closest sine-multiscroll literature concerns inequivalent vector fields.
residual_risks: A non-indexed or inaccessible follow-up could conceivably contain the same source-specific census; none was identified in the title-, DOI-, coefficient-, coordinate-, or implication-based searches performed.

The source's displayed Cramer-rule decimal determinants are rounded, so the accepted proof intentionally derives from the exact printed vector field coefficients rather than from those rounded determinant numerators.

value.rationale: The source explicitly links its multiscroll dynamics to motion among multiple unstable equilibria but leaves that organizing set uncounted. A complete equilibrium census and Morse-index split at the headline chaotic parameter point is a natural dynamical invariant: it distinguishes the three observed scrolls from the much larger saddle skeleton and provides exact input for future bifurcation, connecting-orbit, and basin analyses. The result is not a cosmetic recomputation of a listed table; the total count and 26/27 index partition are absent from the source.
